summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain and found to have diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 764 and mild anion gap metabolic acidosis. She was treated with IV insulin and fluids, which resolved the DKA. During the hospitalization, she reported pain with port access, and imaging revealed a kinked catheter consistent with pinch-off syndrome. She underwent successful removal of the dysfunctional right subclavian port and placement of a new double-lumen port in the left internal jugular vein. Her pain was managed per her care contract, and electrolyte imbalances, including low magnesium and calcium, were corrected. She stabilized clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with updated insulin instructions, continued pain medications, and follow-up planned with her primary care provider for medication renewal and smoking cessation support.
